title: ‘Pervert glasses’ named Macquarie Dictionary’s 2026 Word of the Year
excerpt: Judges and the Australian public have agreed that so-called smart glasses are anything but.
content_html:
Judges and the Australian public have agreed that so-called smart glasses are anything but.

The keepers of Australia’s national lexicon, alongside a world-weary public, have chosen the 2026 Macquarie Dictionary Word of the Year.

Pervert glasses: plural noun Colloquial camera glasses; smart glasses.

You’re out of free articles for this month

To continue reading the rest of this article, please log in.

Named for the rather onerous habit of filming people without their permission or knowledge, the term beat out terms such as agentic, digital dementia, Marrickville pause (the pause dwellers in Sydney’s inner west take when a passenger jet roars past on its way to Sydney International; a pause this author is very aware of), and nudify to take the top spot.

“The coinage pervert glasses is a succinct reflection of the state of the world in 2026 in so many ways,” the dictionary’s committee said in a statement.

“On the one hand, we’ve seen a massive acceleration in the capabilities of AI and products that integrate it. At the same time, the undeniably critical nickname mirrors the widespread calls to hit the brakes on this seemingly unchecked development.

“The name represents the year we’ve all endured, with AI, the manosphere, increasing surveillance in supermarkets, and more. Sure, these new gadgets might be marketed as smart glasses or camera glasses, but it seems to us that pervert glasses paints a more apt reflection of the year.”

AI slop, enshittification, cozzie livs, and bachelor’s handbag have all made the cut in previous years.

Not-for-profit community organisation GetUp! called for a ban on smart glasses after an $89 model proved popular earlier this year, with stock practically running off the shelves.

“Researchers at the University of Sydney pulled 350 smart-glasses videos off Instagram. Around 60 per cent of the covert ones were classified as potential harassment. Women filmed without knowing. Faces posted for strangers to rate. Everyday people are being turned into content without their consent,” GetUp! said in September.

“We need stronger federal regulations, and the Australian government is currently consulting on changes to the Privacy Act. With digital safety and privacy experts, we’re pushing hard for legislative protections that address the risks of emerging technologies like camera glasses. But the legislation will take time, and the glasses are still on the shelf today.”

Agentic and Marrickville pause were the two other contenders, from a voting shortlist of 19.

“While it might not be the most flashy, funny, or socially impactful word on the surface, agentic has seen an exponential increase in usage over the last 12 months,” the committee said.

“Where 2024 and 2025 saw the development and massive spread of large language models, the release of agentic AI tools such as OpenClaw and the mischief they recently wrought has brought this otherwise very technical term firmly into the mainstream.”
